meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Estado español; single national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental-notarial system; unitary national commercial legislation integrated with EU law)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April 2010 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 of 27 April 2021 (5th EU AML Directive transposition) and Law 18/2022 of 28 September 2022; implementing Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May 2014; Single Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro Único de Titularidades Reales) established by the Sole Additional Provision of Royal Decree-Law 7/2021, developed by Order JUS/319/2022 of 22 April 2022; beneficial owner identification rules under Article 4.2(a) of Law 10/2010 requiring declaration of any direct or indirect holding of at least 25% of capital or voting rights, or control by other means; UBO statements of the SL are executed before a Spanish notary and inscribed with the Mercantile Registry in accordance with Articles 204, 235 and 236 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010) and the Mercantile Registry Regulation (Royal Decree 1784/1996 of 23 December 1996).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or registry extract of the non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or commercial register of the shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Apostille Convention (in force for Spain since 18 September 1978); consular legalization required if the issuing state is not a Hague Contracting Party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (certificado de vigencia) of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original commercial registry or competent supervisory authority of the shareholder's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization consistent with the document's country of origin; sworn Spanish translation must be appended

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (poder notarial) appointing the Spanish incorporation agent or managing director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the notarial act; sworn translation into Spanish to be inserted in or annexed to the Spanish notarial deed

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Consolidated Spanish Capital Companies Act, Ley de Sociedades de Capital – LSC), Articles 20–23 (incorporation formalities), 22 as amended by Ley 18/2022 (minimum capital abolished), 27 (legal reserve), 33 (legal personality upon registration), 62 (registration of deed), and 209–211 (appointment of administrators); Ley 19/2013, Article 33 (obligatory Interest Groups Register).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, Madrid) for the name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the registered office for final inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) executed before a Spanish Notary, presented to the Registro Mercantil Provincial together with Form D-1 for registration and proof of settlement of the transfer tax (ITP-AJD).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under Ley 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), the minimum €3,000 capital quota for S.L. is abolished. The incorporation deed may provide a statutory capital from €1, fully subscribed and paid in cash at the time of execution. The legal reserve regime (Art. 27 LSC) nevertheless requires allocation of 20% of annual profits until the paid-in capital plus legal reserve reaches €3,000. Bank escrow account rules apply only to non-cash contributions; cash contributions are evidenced by the notarial statement of payment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FOR THE RECORD, the founding shareholders and sole director of [●], S.L., hereby RESOLVE: (1) Ratification. The public deed of incorporation executed before Notary Public on [●] is ratified, and all share subscriptions comprising the entire stated capital are confirmed as subscribed and paid. (2) Registered Office. The registered office is established at [●], Madrid, Spain, serving as legal, fiscal and administrative domicile. (3) Officers. [Full Name] is appointed Sole Administrator and [Full Name] is appointed Non-Director Secretary, both accepting their offices forthwith. (4) Delegation. The Administrator is authorized to open bank accounts, procure the definitive NIF, perfect registration in all public registries, obtain municipal and sector-specific licenses, and execute any ancillary corporate documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Corporate Name (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid – telematic application portal of the Colegio de Registradores de España.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the name application electronically for a negative denomination certificate, confirming that the proposed corporate name including 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' does not coincide with or resemble an existing entity. The certificate is valid for three months. Pay the prescribed registry tariff via the integrated payment gateway.
required_dossiers: Completed name-application form identifying the promoters
Copies of passport or national ID of each founding shareholder
Declaration of the intended statutory object (ISIC 7020 / lobbying advisory)
Proof of payment of the official name-certificate fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused or subject to a prior conflicting entry, file a substitute application with alternative names; no formal appeal is needed for a negative certificate and re-application can be made on the same day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation Before Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) located within the province of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the valid negative name certificate to the chosen notary together with the drafted articles of association (estatutos). The notary verifies party identity and capacity, confirms the capital subscription and full cash payment, and reads and executes the deed. The notary then transmits digitally to the competent provincial commercial registry and issues a first copy (primera copia) to the incorporators.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (valid 3 months)
Draft articles of association (bylaws) compliant with LSC standard model
Passport/NIF of each shareholder and director
Payment certification of capital contribution (notary declaration)
Ultimate beneficial ownership statement and professional data of the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution due to defects in the draft, correct the identified clauses and re-execute as a new instrument; alternatively use the official simplified incorporation guidelines to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Settlement of Capital Transfer Tax (ITP-AJD) and Provisional NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and the Treasury of the competent Autonomous Community (for ITP-AJD).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 working days of the deed, lodge Model 600 for the surety tax on corporate transactions (operaciones societarias) with the regional tax office, and submit Model 036 to the AEAT requesting the provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF). The provisional NIF enables opening bank accounts and completing he registry filing.
required_dossiers: First copy of the incorporation deed
Model 600 completed with deed fiscal data
Model 036 (censo de empresarios) with promoter identification
Certification of ownership structure for beneficial ownership analysis
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On administrative query, present the sealed deed and the AEAT acknowledgement receipt; unpaid taxes payable with statutory late-interest under Ley 58/2003; the definitive NIF conversion may still proceed after tax regularization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial first copy, completed D-1 registration application, ITP-AJD settlement evidence and the tax appointment. The registrar examines legality; once registered, the company acquires separate legal personality (LSC Art. 33). Confirm the inscription by obtaining a certified extract (certificación de inscripción).
required_dossiers: First copy of the incorporation deed
Form D-1 of the Mercantile Registry
Proof of settlement of ITP-AJD (Model 600 receipt)
Provisional NIF from AEAT
Payment receipt for registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a calificación desfavorable (negative qualification), file a remedy of subsanación before the same registry providing corrected documents, or appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) under the Mercantile Registry Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF, Social Security Enrollment and Municipal Opening Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT (local tax office), Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and the Ayuntamiento (municipal council) of the office location.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription, present the registry certificate to AEAT to convert the NIF to definitive status (Model 036 update). Register the employer with TGSS obtaining an Código de Cuenta de Cotización and enroll the administration. File the municipal declaración responsable de inicio de actividad or obtain the licencia de apertura for professional offices according to the local by-laws.
required_dossiers: Registry inscription certificate and qualifying filing
Definitive NIF confirmation from AEAT
Lease contract or property title for the offices
Fire-safety and structural clearance certificates
Occupational risk prevention statement (Ley 31/1995)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal notices of non-compliance require submission of corrective technical documentation within 10 working days; administrative silence after the stated period allows the commencement of activity where the municipal operation presumes consent; TGSS corrections are remedied through the Red.sistema RED or written re-instatement request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Interest Groups Registration and Lobbying Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oficina de Conflictos de Intereses, Ministerio de Hacienda – Registro de Grupos de Interés (central State registry), with regional registries as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the Interest Groups Register kept in application of Law 19/2013, declaring the lobbying activity relating to cross-border trade policy and foreign stakeholder representation. Provide the corporate data, the specific subjects matter of the lobbying activities, the public administrations and offices held monitored, and the estimated annual budget of activity. Maintain an updated declaration every time the object or means change.
required_dossiers: Corporate registry certificate of the S.L.
Description of lobbying scope and target public bodies
Identification of legal representatives conducting the activity
List of public policies subject of interest
Annual budget estimate for interest representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the register requires clarifications, submit the corrected statements; failure to update entails material penalties under the Transparency Law, remedied by prompt supplementary filing and rectification of the activity report.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industria y de la Pequeña y Mediana Empresa (Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism) jointly with the municipal licensing authority (Ayuntamiento) having territorial jurisdiction of the office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura or Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad for service-provider offices (administrative advisory activity, ISIC 7020), together with mandatory enrollment in the Registro de Grupos de Interés of Law 19/2013 and, where applicable, authorization as a professional collaborator of foreign entities pursuant to the Service Directive.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) and the environmental authority of the Autonomous Community where the offices are located.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 'D' – Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment under Law 21/2013, Annex II: administrative office and consultation activities produce no significant environmental effect. A municipal environmental communication or integration permit (comunicación ambiental previa) suffices where the premises exceed 300 m² or are in a protected area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions arise from office activity. Domestic discharges must comply with municipal sewerage by-laws: pH 6.0–9.5, suspended solids ≤ 500 mg/L, COD ≤ 1,600 mg/L, and BOD5 ≤ 750 mg/L. Waste management: non-hazardous office waste recycled per Royal Decree 1055/2022; waste electrical and electronic equipment managed through authorized take-back schemes under Royal Decree 110/2015.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) issued by the municipal technical inspection service or an authorized collaboration entity; structural load and occupancy clearance for premises over 300 m² or with a capacity exceeding 50 persons; workplace safety and health surveillance plan (Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales) covering the office, ergonomics, electrical installation, and emergency evacuation; and municipal accessibility clearance (Real Decreto 505/2007).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must first obtain a N.I.F. (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for the company. The procedure is: (1) apply for a provisional CIF/NIF via the AEAT before notarising the deed of incorporation, or alternatively obtain a definitive NIF after registration in the Mercantile Registry; (2) file Form 036/037 (Censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) to be registered in the Census of Economic Activities and obtain the definitive VAT identification number (NIF-IVA). For EU entities a valid EU VAT ID may suffice for intra-community operations, but for a branch or permanent establishment a Spanish NIF is mandatory. Bank account proof, notarised incorporation deed, and power of attorney are generally required; an online electronic certificate (certificado electrónico) is needed for digital filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada are separate taxable persons (contribuyentes del Impuesto sobre Sociedades) and are not pass-through entities. Profits are taxed at the corporate income tax rate (currently 25%, with 15% for newly created entities in the first two years of taxable profits under certain conditions). Shareholders are separately taxed on distributions. The entity is also a taxable person for VAT (IVA) purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under Spanish tax law there is no direct 'check-the-box' election. Relevant election mechanisms include: (a) the 'consolidaciôn fiscal' election available to groups of companies meeting the 70% shareholding threshold and other requirements (articles 67-77 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law 27/2014); (b) the option under article 61 of the same law to include or exclude certain tax credits and deductions; (c) the option for the general regime versus the simplified regime for small enterprises and the special regime for new entities (15% rate election); and (d) hybrid mismatch structuring is strictly constrained by the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) as transposed in the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law, with mandatory disclosure obligations for aggressive tax planning. A foreign shareholder cannot unilaterally elect to ignore the SL's legal personality for tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_notes: The SL is also automatically a permanent establishment of its foreign parent if the parent conducts business in Spain through it, subject to Spanish non-resident income tax attribution rules where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_consolidation_group_option: Eligible groups may elect to file consolidated corporate income tax returns, allowing intra-group losses and income set-offs, subject to the 70% direct/indirect voting rights threshold and uniform accounting period requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.standard_headline_rate_notes: Reduced rates apply: 10% (certain foodstuffs, housing, tourist services), 4% (basic necessities). A 0% level applies in Ceuta and Melilla, which are outside EU VAT territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Spain does not require VAT registration solely on the basis of turnover for habitual entrepreneurs; registration is obligatory from the first taxable supply (no universal general exemption threshold comparable to the UK £85k). However, small businesses with an annual volume of operations not exceeding EUR 250,000 may elect the Simplified Regime (régimen simplificado), under which VAT liability is determined via module/flat-rate formulas. For non-established (foreign) suppliers selling to Spanish non-taxable persons in excess of €10,000 annually via electronic interfaces, the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) special regime may apply. For B2B services, reverse charge applies without registration if the recipient is registered; but for physical business presence or local operations, full Spanish NIF-IVA registration is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates electronic invoicing for B2B transactions through the 'Verifactura' system and the Crea y Crece law (Law 18/2022) effective from 2024 for business-to-business e-invoicing for entities with annual turnover over EUR 8 million, and later for all entities. The mandate requires structured electronic invoices (JSON/XML) with a digital fingerprint (hash) and end-to-end integrity, and the use of approved software providers. Real-time fiscal clearance (similar to Spanish 'TicketBAI' system) is already compulsory in the Basque Country and parts of Navarre; nationwide 'Verifactura' will require real-time reporting to AEAT or qualified software platforms. Foreign entities issuing invoices in Spain must comply with data content requirements (full NIF, invoice serial number, dates, base, tax amounts) and, where applicable, use qualified electronic signatures.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.vat_group_registration_election: Spain permits VAT grouping ('Grupo de IVA') with a single VAT number for a group of closely related entities established in Spain, effective for continuous tax periods, subject to prior registration and compliance; this election is not automatic and requires AEAT approval.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.intra_community_acquisition_rules: Intra-community acquisitions of goods by a Spanish SL are subject to VAT in Spain (reverse charge) when the supplier is an EU taxable person; no additional IVA registration is needed if the recipient has a Spanish NIF-IVA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.reverse_charge_mechanism: Reverse charge (inversión del sujeto pasivo) applies generally to B2B supplies of services located in Spain, to certain construction and real estate transactions, and to supplies of goods under specific chapters; foreign service suppliers are relieved from Spanish VAT registration for B2B services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to third countries (outside the EU) are zero-rated (exempt with right to deduction) under article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law, provided the goods physically leave the EU within the legally established periods and are supported by documentary evidence. Supplies of services directly connected to export of goods (e.g., logistics, packing) may also be zero-rated. Exemptions for intra-community supplies (article 25) apply when the buyer is registered with a valid EU VAT ID and goods are transported within the EU. Offshore services rendered by the Spanish SL to foreign clients are generally zero-rated if the place of supply is outside Spain (B2B under Article 69-70 of the VAT Law), provided the counterparty is a taxable person outside the EU or in another EU territory under reverse charge rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Documento Único Administrativo (DUA) / Single Administrative Document (SAD) – customs export declaration with the unique movement reference number (MRN)
Commercial invoice issued by the Spanish exporter (factura comercial)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or AWB (air waybill) evidencing physical departure of goods from EU customs territory
Delivery/acceptance proof including the recipient's signature, warehouse receipts, or customs stamped documents
Evidence of payment and Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de remesa de entrada) issued by the Spanish bank or SWIFT/MT103 confirmation for proof of receipt of foreign currency
For intra-community supplies: the customer's valid EU VAT registration number and periodic recapitulative statement (modelo 349)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_notes: For export-related foreign currency proceeds, Spain's VAT regulations require that the export be economically complete and documented; while there is no strict statutory forex repatriation deadline in the VAT Law itself, the AEAT will generally expect receipt of payment within 180 days for the zero-rating to be substantiated. For corporate income tax purposes, exchange control rules under CNMV/Bank of Spain regulations require incoming foreign investment/export proceeds to be received within the standard 180-day commercial period; failure can trigger clawback of the tax benefit.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may retrospectively correct improperly zero-rated exports and recover unpaid VAT plus interest. Penalties range from 50% to 150% of the tax avoided for 'infracción tributaria' (Tax Law General, ley 58/2003). In fraudulent export schemes, criminal tax fraud penalties under the Spanish Criminal Code apply, including imprisonment for amounts exceeding EUR 120,000 (art. 305). Additionally, false or incomplete customs declarations attract customs penalties under Spanish Customs Law (Ley 19/2020), and the exporter may lose eligibility for simplification or suspension of registration. Substantiation documentation must be retained for four years plus, in practice, at least five years from the end of the filing period.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.export_refund_mechanism: Exported goods generally give rise to a refund of input VAT (VAT included in purchases) after the export is evidenced; the overdue refund request (solicitud de devolución) may be made via AEAT Form 303/390 or by special monthly refund regime; for non-established taxable persons, the EU VAT Refund Directive procedures apply via the corresponding Spanish portal.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.export_zero_vat_rate_confirmation: Spain applies '0% VAT with right to deduction' for exports (exención plena), not a literal zero percentage line; this status is intended to result in a full refund of all attributable input VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting jointly with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) of the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio, for foreign-investment registration and balance-of-payments statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone Member State and the euro is fully convertible. Under TFEU Articles 63–66, capital and payment movements between Spain, other EU Member States, and qualifying third countries are fully liberalised. No exchange-control approval is required for current-account transactions, dividend distributions, profit remittance, royalty payments, or liquidation proceeds. Profit repatriation from an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is permitted without convertibility restrictions, subject to corporate validation: audited financial statements where legally required, a shareholders' resolution confirming the dividend or reduction of capital, satisfaction of the capital-maintenance test, and no outstanding tax liabilities to the Agencia Tributaria. All transfers to non-residents above the annual statistical threshold of EUR 1,000,000 must be reported through the Banco de España's balance-of-payments declarations. Payments originating from or destined to non-cooperative tax jurisdictions or jurisdictions under FATF enhanced monitoring may receive additional AML scrutiny but remain legally convertible.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory surrender requirements on export proceeds or service revenues in foreign currency. There is no mandatory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio to euro. Exporters and service providers may maintain collections in foreign-currency accounts or hedge them freely through authorised credit institutions. The Spanish SL is required to support any inward remittance from a non-resident with the underlying invoice, contract, and, where applicable, proof of service delivery, so that the receiving bank can satisfy anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening. Where the aggregate annual volume of transactions with non-residents exceeds EUR 1,000,000, the SL must file the corresponding statistical declaration with the Banco de España.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Client Retainer Collection Account / Operating Disbursement Account
Client Retainer Collection Account / Treasury Settlement Account
Operational Account with Segregated Regulatory Escrow Sub-Account
Operating Account for Retainer Collections and Professional Fee Disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EU-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) that hold a valid passport under PSD2 and are registered with the Banco de España or are operating through a branch; Low for offshore, non-EEA digital EMIs without a Spanish or EU banking licence. A non-EU EMI cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to the Spanish SL unless it establishes a Spanish branch or partners with an EU-licensed payment institution. For the ISIC 7020 government-affairs lobbying activity, tier-1 credit institutions are recommended over EMI rails because of the statutory-licence requirement, enhanced PEP exposure, and the need for auditable correspondent-banking trails. When EMI rails are used, the SL must ensure that the EMI maintains a segregated safeguarding account and that incoming retainer wires can be traced to the ultimate client for AML and conflict-of-interest reviews.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Spanish banks generally mandate an in-person onboarding interview for corporate entities with non-resident shareholders and a medium-risk political-exposure profile. The statutory director or at least two authorised signatories must appear physically at a branch in Spain for the initial KYC interview, presenting original passports, proof of address, and the notarised articles of association. Remote onboarding is permitted only select banks using high-grade video identification, but the corporate deed, power of attorney, and supporting documents must be notarised, apostilled, and translated by a sworn translator into Spanish. For a lobbying and government-affairs advisory SL, at least one physical encounter with the compliance officer is strongly recommended to satisfy the bank's reputational-risk assessment. Following activation, signatory powers of attorney may allow remote treasury operations without repeated travel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a non-EU resident or is in a high-risk third country
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate extract from the home registry, notarised UBO declaration, source-of-wealth statement, certified passport copies, EU tax-residence certificate or equivalent, a negative sanctions and PEP screening, and a corroborating legal opinion from the incorporating counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business scope is 'government affairs and lobbying' and directors may be treated as politically exposed persons (PEPs)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid domestic lobbying registration licence or exemption certificate, documented client engagement contracts, detailed fee schedule, written compliance and conflicts-of-interest policies, anti-bribery training records, PEP clearance for all shareholders and directors, and a forensic accounting opinion confirming no capitation or corruption-linked revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to foreign public-affairs consultants or sub-agents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed consultancy agreements with clearly defined deliverables, KYC files and beneficial-ownership details of each payee, sanctions and adverse-media screening reports, timesheets or activity reports evidencing real services, tax invoices satisfying Spanish invoicing rules, and an authorised payment-matrix signed by two directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance mismatch between forecast retainer revenue and minimal staff or physical premises
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for registered office and administrative space in Spain, employment contracts plus social security registrations (alta en la Seguridad Social), corporate tax references and VAT filings, audited or internally prepared financial projections, and a bank reference letter from the source of capital.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound capital injections from non-resident shareholders into the Spanish SL, the standard compliant rail is a SWIFT MT103 through a licensed credit institution. The sending bank must include the company's Spanish NIF, the beneficiary IBAN (starting 'ES'), and the SWIFT UETR for end-to-end traceability. The remittance narrative must state the purpose as 'Aportación de capital social / Capital increase' for equity injections or 'Préstamo entre empresas / Intercompany loan' for shareholder financing. Equity injections should be contemporaneous with the notarial deed of capital increase and the subsequent filing at the Mercantile Registry; if the investment exceeds EUR 3,000,000, or if the investor is a non-EU entity in a screened sector, the DGCIIN foreign-investment registration must be completed under applicable Spanish FDI rules. For operational retainer inflows, the incoming wire purpose code should be 'Servicios profesionales / Professional services' and the bank must hold a signed retainer contract and KYC file for the foreign client. All inbound wires must be accompanied by a currency declaration to the bank and, where applicable, a balance-of-payments statistical filing for annual flows above EUR 1,000,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade and service settlement, the SL will use SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR for EU/EEA transactions of lower value, and SWIFT MT103 for international payments, especially retainer fees to foreign law firms, government-relations consultants, and trade-policy analysts. For USD-denominated payments, the correspondent clearing rail is typically Fedwire or CHIPS through the bank's US correspondents; for EUR, TARGET2 is used; and for other currencies the bank may use SWIFT gpi correspondent banking with continuous tracking. A commercial letter of credit is only appropriate where the underlying activity involves tangible goods, which is not the natural case for ISIC 7020 advisory and lobbying services; where required for ancillary procurements, it may be issued by a tier-1 bank with conformity documents such as invoices, insurance certificates, and customs declarations. To prevent compliance holds, each outgoing MT103 must carry the purpose description 'Professional services — government affairs consultancy', supported by the invoice, the contract, and the recipient's bank and KYC details. The SL should maintain a register of all outward wires with the corresponding UETR and SWIFT gpi tracker.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP deliverable FX forwards executed with a Banco de España-authorised credit institution
FX swaps (swap de divisas) for short-term treasury liquidity conversion and refinancing of currency exposures
Cross-currency swaps for long-dated foreign-currency retainer receivables or intercompany loan exposures
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible emerging-market currencies where no onshore deliverable forward exists
FX options and collars entered into under MiFID II suitability rules for genuine commercial hedging, with no speculative leverage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts filing (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval, which must occur within 6 months of fiscal year-end (latest July 31 for a 31 December fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Closure of the company's registration folio, preventing further valid filings; administrative fines from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000; possible compulsory strike-off after 2 consecutive years of non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 days and 6 months after fiscal year-end (latest July 25 for a 31 December fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge from 5% to 20% plus late-payment interest; civil penalty up to 150% of the tax shortfall; minimum penalty of EUR 300 for filings with no amount due.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / Registro de Titularidades Reales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the annual accounts filing, normally one month after shareholder approval (latest July 31 for a 31 December fiscal year); also required within one month of any change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Law 10/2010 of up to EUR 60,000 for serious infringement; registry record blocking and suspension of corporate filings until regularized.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with Modelo 200 (latest July 25 for a 31 December fiscal year), applicable when related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial penalty of EUR 200 per omitted or incorrect data item with a minimum penalty of EUR 5,000 under Article 198 of the General Tax Law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the SL meets at least two of the following three criteria for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average workforce above 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, R.D. 1514/2007 as amended by R.D. 602/2016). Consolidated financial statements of listed groups use EU-adopted IFRS; non-listed groups use the consolidated PGC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must file an annual UBO confirmation to the Mercantile Registry together with the annual accounts, identifying every individual or entity with more than 25% shareholding, voting rights, or ultimate control. Any change in UBO details must be filed within one month of the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 – USD 2,500 per year (approx. EUR 650 – EUR 2,300), depending on commercial agent and physical office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 12,000 per year (approx. EUR 3,200 – EUR 11,000), depending on company size and transaction complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created entities on first €300,000 of taxable base for first two years with positive tax base; R&D and innovation tax credits; deductions for job creation and export activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically via AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., for calendar year-end, by July 25).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number (NIF) of the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Spanish NIF assigned to the SL; non-resident shareholders not required on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Standard calendar year unless otherwise approved.
Report based on Spanish GAAP; adjust for permanent and temporary differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent differences (e.g., non-deductible expenses, exempt income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include disallowed lobbying expenses if not properly documented.
Apply Spanish tax depreciation rules; no special non-resident treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before offset of tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute after adjustments; non-resident shareholders not directly involved.
Indefinite carryforward, but limited to 70% of taxable base for entities with turnover < €20 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate applied (25% standard, 15% for new entities on first €300,000).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select applicable rate; new entity status must be verified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and deductions (e.g., R&D, double taxation relief).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only if eligible; maintain supporting documentation.
Final amount after credits and prepayments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months; plus late payment interest (currently 3.75% per annum). Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due, and €1,000 for incorrect data.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must submit Form 210 (Non-Resident Income Tax Return) to claim refund or apply reduced withholding. Provide Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from home jurisdiction to the Spanish paying entity before dividend distribution. For EU/EEA residents, Parent-Subsidiary Directive may exempt withholding if holding ≥5% for ≥1 year. Application via AEAT with supporting TRC and shareholding evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 24% (reduced to 19% for EU residents under Interest and Royalties Directive, subject to conditions). Interest: statutory 19% (0% for EU residents under directive if beneficial owner and no permanent establishment in Spain). Treaty rates may further reduce (e.g., US-Spain treaty: 10% on royalties, 5% on interest).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Entities with net turnover ≥ €10 million must prepare Master File and Local File. For entities below threshold, documentation required only if related-party transactions exceed €250,000 per counterparty or €1 million in aggregate. Additionally, all transactions with tax havens must be documented regardless of amount.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) but applies general anti-abuse rules (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles. For tax residency, entities must have real economic activity (premises, employees, management) in Spain. Treaty benefits may be denied if no substance. Lobbying activities must be substantiated with contracts, invoices, and evidence of actual services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, inflating expenses, or falsifying records related to lobbying fees or government contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax evaded, plus late payment interest. Criminal prosecution for amounts exceeding €120,000 per year, leading to imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and fine of up to 6 times the evaded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts if they caused or contributed to the evasion. Criminal liability extends to directors, with potential travel bans and asset freezes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a shell entity with no real employees, premises, or business activity, used solely to channel funds or obtain tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of income, denial of treaty benefits, and imposition of 25% penalty on deemed income. Administrative dissolution of the company and cancellation of tax registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for corporate tax liabilities if they knowingly operated a sham entity. Travel bans and prohibition on holding directorships for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML controls, accepting cash payments over €10,000, or engaging in transactions with politically exposed persons (PEPs) without due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €150,000 for serious infractions, and up to €1.5 million for very serious infractions. Criminal charges for money laundering with imprisonment of 1 to 6 years and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be criminally liable for AML breaches, with personal fines and imprisonment. Travel bans and restrictions on managing financial entities.
